description: Mapping from the legacy CyrillicaBgEpigraphMod 8-bit font encoding to Unicode (Cyrillic, Cyrillic Supplement, Combining Cyrillic, Old Cyrillic, and generic combining diacritics). The legacy documents were saved under several different code pages, so the same font byte surfaces as different characters depending on how a given file was decoded. Both views are provided: 'mapping' is keyed by character (use it on already-decoded text, whatever the decoding was), and 'byte_mapping' is keyed by raw byte value (use it when reading bytes directly).
notes: Every key is a single character and every byte key is a single byte, so a plain per-character substitution is enough; no longest-match logic is needed.

Targets may be more than one character (a base letter plus one or two combining marks), so use str.maketrans + str.translate, which accepts multi-character replacements, rather than a fixed-width byte table.

The character keys were cross-checked against the byte table: every key decodes to the same legacy byte under at least one of the listed code pages, and no byte receives two different targets. The 'legacy_byte' and 'seen_as_decoding' fields in 'entries' record which byte and which decoding each key came from.
U+2219 BULLET OPERATOR is the one key with no byte assignment; it is a variant form of U+00B7 MIDDLE DOT (byte 0xB7) and maps to the same target.

Bytes 0x80-0x9F carry real glyphs in this font. Under latin-1 they decode to C1 controls, under cp1250/cp1251/cp1252/cp1253 to typographic punctuation (curly quotes, dashes, dagger, per-mille) and under cp1250/cp1251 to letters such as Ђ, Ѓ, Љ, Њ, Ќ, Џ. All of those forms are present as keys.
Bytes with no mapping (space, , - . : ; < > [ \ ] j { | } ~ DEL and 0xA0) are not font glyphs and should be passed through unchanged, as should any character not found in the table.

Apply this only to text that was actually set in CyrillicaBgEpigraphMod (the <CYR> runs that convert_i.pl tags from FACE="CyrillicaBgEpigraphMod"). Ordinary Cyrillic letters are themselves keys and map to different letters (for example Е to U+0454, О to U+047B, И to U+0457), so running this over normal Russian prose will corrupt it.

Targets are not normalized: some are given decomposed (U+0406 U+0308 for Ї, U+0456 U+0308 for ї). Apply unicodedata.normalize('NFC', s) afterwards for composed forms. The combining Cyrillic letters in U+2DE0-U+2DFF have no composed equivalents, so NFC leaves them alone, which is correct.
One target contains U+200D ZERO WIDTH JOINER (the а-у digraph); keep it, it is carrying the ligature.
The mapping is many-to-one and therefore not invertible.
